object_types.name: Shipment
object_types.definition: A consignment of products moved through the network and stored in warehouses.

source_references.excerpt: We track shipments -- consignments, some of the older staff say, same thing. Each shipment has a shipment number.

object_types.name: ShipmentNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a shipment.

source_references.excerpt: Each shipment has a shipment number.
For example, shipment S-100 contains product P-77 in quantity 5.

object_types.name: Quantity

ambiguities.description: Identification of Shipment: The transcript states 'Each shipment has a shipment number' but does not clarify whether the shipment number is internally generated (e.g., auto_counter) or externally assigned. The example 'S-100' suggests a formatted text identifier, but the generation mechanism is not specified. Is this a simple incrementing number, a coded scheme, or something else?

ambiguities.description: Identification of Product: The transcript states products are 'identified by SKU' but does not clarify whether the SKU is a self-contained identifier (text code like 'P-77') or composite. The example 'P-77' suggests a simple text code. Is SKU the only identifier, or could there be an alternative identifier such as product name or EAN?

ambiguities.description: Optionality of Product in Shipment: The model constrains each Shipment-Product pair to have exactly one Quantity, but does not explicitly state whether every Shipment must contain at least one Product. Can a shipment exist with no products? The phrase 'A shipment contains products' (plural) may imply at least one, but is not definitive.
